title: Pending review staging suppresses feedback already raised on the pull request

provenance.originSummary: Sanitized from a live staging run that repeated two exact suggestions already posted by another reviewer.
provenance.whyItMattered: Repeated review comments create noise, split one concern across competing threads, and make maintainers appear inattentive to existing contributor discussion.
provenance.genericCondition: A frozen audit contains concerns that are materially equivalent to existing inline threads, submitted review bodies, or top-level pull request discussion, while at least one genuinely new concern remains.
provenance.notes: The fixture uses generic paths and synthetic identifiers; no real pull request or service name is retained.

description: A staging run retrieves complete existing feedback, suppresses exact and semantic duplicates across feedback surfaces, and previews only genuinely new feedback.

scope.notes: The synthetic pull request exposes complete paginated review-thread, review-body, and discussion-comment history.

mustCatch.description: The workflow retrieves all review threads with replies and state, submitted review bodies, and top-level discussion comments before preview.
An exact suggestion-only thread is recognized as substantive equivalent feedback and suppresses the duplicate staging candidate.
A resolved thread with different wording but the same concern and correction suppresses the equivalent candidate.
Equivalent feedback in a submitted review body suppresses a candidate even without an inline anchor.
Suppression changes only staging eligibility and leaves every frozen audit finding unchanged.
A genuinely new concern remains eligible and produces exactly one staged inline comment.
The Request Changes Summary contains only the unsuppressed blocking finding.
The complete existing-feedback comparison is repeated after approval and before atomic creation.

mustNotFlag.description: Duplicate detection must not require matching prose when the concern and correction path are materially equivalent.
Resolved or outdated equivalent feedback must not be ignored merely because its thread state changed.
Suppressing staged feedback must not remove or rewrite the immutable audit baseline.
The distinct delete-path finding must not be suppressed by unrelated existing feedback.

mustIncludeMarkers: Could we keep this assignment behind the existing-version guard instead?
Existing feedback recheck before mutation: complete and unchanged
mustNotIncludeMarkers: Would it make sense to use `errors.New` here?

notes: This adjudicated case protects the existing-feedback deduplication gate across inline threads, review bodies, and staging revalidation.
